sections.name: summary
sections.label: In short
sections.content: Most work happens in short-term memory: small contexts, one task. Long-term memory is what survives, placed where it can be found again.

sections.name: body
sections.label: The evidence
sections.content: The owner, 2026-10-30: "Short term and long term memory are different things. We generally operate in short term memory, focussed on smaller contexts." Earlier, 2026-10-27 (c8b12a7b): meaning is temporal, and the dream cycle turns short-term memory into long-term memory. srs-context is layered this way: a brief always loaded, then the system map, decisions, conventions and concepts, then findings and the journal. The navigability topic thread (2bf30967) holds the owner's discussion of layered memory and the maintenance skill.

sections.name: open
sections.label: Open
sections.content: Which of our repositories have a short-term layer (journal, vignettes, session notes) and which go straight to long-term records?
